title: Mining Subsidies Legislation Amendment (Raising Revenue) Bill 2014
short_title: Mining Subsidies Legislation Amendment (Raising Revenue) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would remove fuel tax credits and several accelerated tax deductions available to mining businesses, including concessions for exploration and resource industry assets.
It would apply 1 January 2015 cut-offs to specified exploration deductions and depreciation concessions, including special asset lives used by oil and gas businesses.
The proposal would target resource companies while leaving equivalent agricultural concessions unchanged, and the Act itself would commence the day after Royal Assent.
changes: Mining and quarrying businesses would lose eligibility to claim fuel tax credits.
Assets first used for exploration or prospecting on or after 1 January 2015 would no longer qualify for immediate deduction.
Selected aircraft and vehicles used in mining would lose capped depreciation lives when the relevant asset time falls on or after 1 January 2015.
Exploration or prospecting expenditure incurred from 1 January 2015 would cease to qualify for the specified company tax deduction.
summary.affected: Mining and quarrying businesses, oil and gas extraction companies and resource companies claiming exploration deductions would be affected.
